record.category: URL-to-host relay for images and video (server fetches, re-hosts, returns a direct link)

free_tier.stated: 'This URL uploader takes a link to an image or video that is already online and uploads it for you. You do not download the file first, and you do not need an account.' Price: Free. Account: Not needed.
free_tier.notes: Batch of up to 40 URLs per upload, one per line.

retention.stated: unverified: the page markets 'a permanent direct link' but publishes no retention period or deletion policy on this page.

egress.terms: Direct links to the re-hosted copy; no byte allowance or hotlink policy stated on this page.

record.interface_detail: A web form taking up to 40 URLs per submit, returning a page link, direct link, embed code, HTML, BBCode and Markdown per file. No API documentation. Allowed types: JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, AVIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, HEIF and MP4, WEBM, AVI.
record.tooling: Browser. The automated path is blocked: a plain HTTP client got HTTP 403 with a challenge signature, so a wrapper needs a real browser session.
record.chaining: It moves an image or clip from a dying host to a live one without using local bandwidth, which is the cheapest fix for hotlink-blocked or expiring media. It is not usable for archives or datasets.

limits.value: 40 URLs per upload; no daily count stated

record.limits_note: The type whitelist is the tighter constraint than either number: no archives, no documents, no audio.
record.binding_note: 200 MB per media file binds long before any count could: a monthly transfer of 1 TiB would need 5,243 files, and any archive over 200 MB cannot pass at all.

identity_cost.detail: 'Account: Not needed' in the feature table, and no login field in the flow.

record.reliability_note: The site refuses non-browser clients (HTTP 403 with a challenge on a plain GET), so unattended use needs a browser driver. Re-hosted copies depend on this operator's retention, which is unpublished.
record.confidence_note: The caps and the type list are quoted from the live page; the 403 is measured. No URL was actually re-hosted, so the flow itself is untested.

evidence.proved: 'Account: Not needed', 'URLs per upload: Up to 40', 'Maximum file size: 200MB per file', and the image/video type whitelist
a plain client is refused: HTTP 403, 5525 bytes, sha256 a2abe9fc99966465..., challenge detected

record.notes: The cleanest anonymous URL-pull found, and the narrowest: media only, 200 MB. It answers 'no install, no account' for one file type class and nothing else.

extras.allowed_types: JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, AVIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, HEIF, MP4, WEBM, AVI
